I've found this to be true for the past year or two now, and I was wondering if anyone has found a better solution than copying context to and from chatgpt.com. The "Pro" level (or whatever the max level is at the time) consistently has better insights than the agent, but immensely limited tool calling compared to the agent. Marrying the two of these together unlocks a lot of potential, but I really just want this intelligence to live on my laptop, instead of me being the intermediary. mickeyp 1 hour ago | next [–] One thing you can try is to build specialised subagents to help tease out more thinking when you're stuck with a model with limited reasoning budget as all the codex sub models seem to be (compared to API) --- but I have no firm, hard evidence of this so treat it as guesswork on my part. Let me explain. Creat a subagent that is told to just mull about a subject. This can be a simple file. Have the agent expound on it with its own thoughts and additions. Now rinse and repeat: give the file to another blank 'reasoning' subagent; then another; and so on. This will eventually reach a point where they are unlikely to add more real value. I believe they've locked down temperature and other sampling parameters so you cannot tweak these to get it to consider more unusual approaches. The absolute best approach is a second model that is of a different family. Try Deepseek, GLM, Qwen, etc. and have it add its own thoughts. As a bonus, these models do not hide their reasoning. Put that in a file also. reply thechairman12 1 hour ago | parent | next [–] Thanks for the response! I like the idea of pitting the various model families against eachother. Mostly because of its overly restrictive auto-mode guardrails and brittle command whitelisting, but also a lot of “oops, I didn’t read the doc that you clearly tell me to read at the top of agents.md, I’ll make an ineffective note so this never happens again (it keeps happening)” The solution I’m using now is various scripts that encapsulate almost everything the agents usually need to do and just whitelist those. reply verdverm 1 hour ago | root | parent [–] I've been working on our custom PR agent at work. The agent phase is minimal, read-only/no bash (except for the .review dir). Most of the effort is in deterministic context gathering with scripts (before), and then posting the lines from a comments.jsonl file (after). I do have to work a something back into the agent phase, such that it can validate the comments.jsonl, because it seems to be generating bad payloads. It's an iterative take-give, take away as much as you can so the bot can focus on the core task, then give some back to improve the agent output as you find repeated mistakes. reply Consider applying for YC's Winter 2027 batch!
